epicTitle: Phase 0 — Design-coherence pass on the Next.js site (token consolidation, single scales, component primitives) with zero visual change
epicBody:
## Goal

Make the current Next.js site *internally coherent* — one token layer, one type scale, one spacing scale, one semantic color layer, and de-duplicated component primitives — **without changing a single rendered pixel or any content**. The cleaned, coherent site then becomes the pixel-perfect spec and the `theme.json` token source for the WordPress rebuild. This work MUST land before the migration, because you cannot faithfully port a design that still contains ~10 competing greens, 2 conflicting token files, ~20 ad-hoc font sizes, and 7 divergent card treatments.

## The one guardrail that makes this safe (read before every slice)

**A token introduced in Phase 0 is a *name for the value that renders today* — never a value change.** Every consolidation resolves to the exact color/size/space currently painted on screen. This is what lets us claim "no visual change" and verify it mechanically.

Concretely:
- Two token files disagree, but only `globals.css` is actually loaded (`layout.tsx` imports only `globals.css`; `tokens.css` is dead code referenced solely by a test). So on any conflict (radius 12/18/24 vs 6/12/18, neutral vs earthy shadows, `#2e7d32` vs `#39A933`), **the canonical value is whatever globals.css renders today** — the live value wins, the dead value is discarded.
- Collapsing near-duplicates (e.g. body sizes 1.02/1.03/1.05/1.06rem → one `--font-size-md`) is allowed only within imperceptible tolerance and is confirmed by screenshot parity.
- Component "consolidation" means **extracting a primitive that reproduces each call site's current output** (variants preserve per-site look). Only byte-identical dead CSS (e.g. `.cta-button`, a duplicate of `.btn.btn-primary`) is deleted outright.

## Explicitly OUT of scope for Phase 0 (these are deliberate visual changes — defer to the WP spec / a design sign-off)

These audit findings are real but each shifts pixels, so they do NOT belong in a no-visual-change refactor: adopting logo-green `#39A933` over live `#2e7d32`; radius 6/12/18 over 12/18/24; the WCAG-AA contrast fixes (white-on-carrot buttons, accent CTA body text); restoring a monotonic h2>h3 desktop step; the hero-title size-ladder rewrite; and correcting the `.main-content` 150px / `.home-main-content` 120px double-inset misalignment. Capture each as a follow-up so the token *names* land now and the value *decisions* are made once, with sign-off, as the first WP theme.json commits.

## Verification discipline (applies to every slice)

Green gate = the existing vitest + Playwright suite passes (`page-shell-tokens`, `heading-contract`, `alignment`, `visual-polish-a11y`, `focus-visible`, the section/renderer/form tests, etc.) **plus** a screenshot-parity check of the key pages (homepage, /abos, a CMS section page, a form page, the 404) showing no diff. The prefactor slice hardens this gate first.

## Prefactor first, then dependency-ordered slices

1. Coherence safety net (token-drift test + parity gate) — **prefactor**
2. Collapse to a single token source of truth
3. Brand-color token layer (green / carrot / beet + tint)
4. Non-brand color token layer (neutrals, surfaces, borders, semantic state)
5. Type scale + weights + line-heights + font-family truth fix
6. Complete spacing scale + route raw-px through it
7. Section vertical-rhythm tokens
8. Button primitive (+ delete duplicate `.cta-button`, shared `ButtonVariant`)
9. SectionHeading primitive across both render paths
10. FormField / input primitives across all six forms
11. Card primitive + card tokens
12. Modal shell primitive
13. De-hardcode RegisteredSectionComponents + enable a hex-literal guard

Slices 3–7 (tokens) can run in parallel once slice 2 lands; slices 8–12 (primitives) can run in parallel once the tokens they consume exist; slice 13 lands last and locks the door.

slices.title: Coherence safety net: token-drift test + screenshot-parity gate
slices.whatToBuild: Before touching any CSS, harden the verification net so every later slice can prove 'no visual change' mechanically. Extend the existing single-source token test so it fails when ANY design token (color/radius/shadow/spacing/font) is defined more than once across the loaded CSS — not just --page-max-width/--page-inline-padding — and so it asserts the real import graph (today tokens.css is concatenated in the test but never imported by the app, masking the dead-code + double-definition problem). Add a lightweight screenshot-parity check (or wire the existing Playwright visual specs) that captures baselines for the homepage, /abos, a CMS section page, a form page, and the 404, to be re-run as the diff gate on every subsequent slice. No production CSS or component changes in this slice.
acceptanceCriteria: The token test fails if a fixture with a duplicate --radius-sm / --font-size-md / any token is introduced, and passes on a clean single-definition set
The test asserts that whatever CSS the app actually loads (per layout.tsx) is the same CSS it validates — a token defined only in an unimported file is flagged as dead, not silently accepted
Screenshot baselines exist for homepage, /abos, one CMS section page, one form page, and the 404, and a documented command re-runs them as a parity diff
Full vitest + Playwright suite is green; zero source CSS/TSX changes in this slice

slices.title: Collapse to a single token source of truth
slices.whatToBuild: Resolve the two-competing-token-files problem with zero runtime effect. Because tokens.css is never imported, the browser only ever sees globals.css's :root — so make ONE canonical :root the single source and remove the dead/duplicate definitions. Keep every currently-rendered value: on each name conflict the live globals.css value wins (radius stays 12/18/24, shadows stay the neutral two-layer set, spacing stays 8/16/24/32/48/64, brand green stays the live #2e7d32) and the divergent tokens.css values are discarded (or tokens.css is deleted). Also remove the stray 1160px shell-width literal in favour of the existing --page-max-width token. This is pure de-duplication: identical output, one place to edit.
acceptanceCriteria: Exactly one :root defines each design token; the token-drift test from slice 1 passes with no duplicate definitions
tokens.css is either deleted or actually imported as the canonical layer — no third state where it exists but is dead; the test enforces this
The 1160px container literal is replaced by a shell-width token; the 1400px-only assertion still holds
Screenshot parity: homepage, /abos, CMS page, form page, 404 are pixel-identical to slice-1 baselines; full suite green
slices.blockedBy: Coherence safety net: token-drift test + screenshot-parity gate

slices.title: Brand-color token layer (green / carrot / beet + tint)
slices.whatToBuild: Give the brand palette a single knob without repainting anything. Define semantic brand tokens — brand (base), brand-dark, brand-soft, brand-tint, carrot (+ strong/soft), beet (+ strong) — each set to the exact value that renders today, then replace brand-color literals with references that resolve to the identical color. Fold the 23 hardcoded rgba(46,125,50,alpha) tints/borders into a color-mix / --color-brand-tint expression that computes the same pixels. Where multiple distinct greens render today (base/dark/soft), keep them as distinct tokens matching their current values — do NOT collapse perceptibly-different greens to one (that value decision is the deferred WP rebrand). Result: changing one token would shift the whole brand, but in this slice nothing shifts.
acceptanceCriteria: Brand green/carrot/beet literals in globals.css route through tokens; the 23 rgba(46,125,50,a) uses derive from the brand token via color-mix and compute byte-equal color
Distinct current greens (e.g. base vs light vs dark) map to distinct tokens equal to their present values — no perceptible green is merged into another
Overriding a brand token in devtools visibly cascades across CTAs/sections (proves indirection), but with tokens at default values the rendered site is pixel-identical to baseline
Screenshot parity + full suite green
slices.blockedBy: Collapse to a single token source of truth

slices.title: Non-brand color token layer: neutrals, surfaces, borders, semantic state
slices.whatToBuild: Tokenize every non-brand color literal to its current value and separate overloaded meanings by NAME only. Define text / text-muted / text-subtle, surface / surface-alt / bg, border, and semantic success / warning / error (+ soft backgrounds), each equal to what renders today, then replace the literal neutrals (#333 x20, #fff x15, #000 x9, plus #999/#c8c8c8/#6b6b6b/#555) and the ad-hoc Bootstrap status hexes with those tokens. Critically, stop the beet accent doubling as error: spots that currently render the beet red keep the beet value under --color-beet, and spots that currently render an error red keep that value under --color-error — the two reds are named apart but neither value changes. Also fold the leaked slate/gray palette (#111827/#94a3b8/#4b5563/#334155/#e5e7eb) onto the neutral tokens at their current values where imperceptible.
acceptanceCriteria: Literal neutrals and status hexes in globals.css (and the React components that re-hardcode them) reference the new tokens; each token equals the value it replaced
Beet-accent usages and error-state usages reference different named tokens, but every affected element renders the same red it does today
Success/warning/error tokens exist with soft-bg variants and are wired to the current validation-state colors
Screenshot parity across the key pages + form validation states; full suite green
slices.blockedBy: Collapse to a single token source of truth

slices.title: Type scale + weights + line-heights + font-family truth fix
slices.whatToBuild: Introduce the modular type system and fix the font-family lie, all at current-rendered values. Define an 8-step --font-size-* scale, --font-weight-* (body/medium/semibold/heading), and --line-height-* (tight/snug/body) tokens whose values match the sizes/weights/line-heights the site paints today. Fix --font-heading/--font-body, which currently name 'Inter' (never loaded), to the real DM Sans stack, and replace the 64 hardcoded 'DM Sans' occurrences with var(--font-body)/var(--font-heading) — output stays DM Sans, so zero visual change. Adopt the size tokens across globals.css and fold the near-duplicate sizes (1.02/1.03/1.05/1.06rem lead copy → one md; 0.85/0.9/0.95rem meta → one sm) within imperceptible tolerance. Do NOT alter the h2/h3 desktop relationship, the hero-title ladder, or the CMS mobile heading overrides in this slice — those are deferred visual decisions; map each to a token equal to its current value.
acceptanceCriteria: --font-size-*, --font-weight-*, --line-height-* tokens exist; the font-family tokens resolve to DM Sans and the 64 literal 'DM Sans' strings are replaced by var() references
globals.css font-size declarations reference the scale; near-duplicate lead/meta sizes are folded and screenshot-diffed as imperceptible

h1/h2/h3, hero-title, and CMS-configurable heading sizes render byte-equal to baseline (their tokens carry current values; the monotonic-hierarchy and hero-ladder fixes are captured as deferred follow-ups, not applied here)
heading-contract, page-header, section-renderer, and visual-polish tests pass; screenshot parity + full suite green
slices.blockedBy: Collapse to a single token source of truth

slices.title: Complete spacing scale + route raw-px through it
slices.whatToBuild: Fill the gaps in the spacing scale and route ad-hoc pixel spacing through tokens without moving anything. Define a complete 4px-based --space-1..12 scale (adding the missing 4px and 12px rungs), and alias the legacy --spacing-xs..2xl names to the equivalent new steps for a non-breaking migration. Then replace on-scale raw-px paddings/margins in globals.css and in inline component styles with the matching token (raw 12px -> --space-3, 16px -> --space-4, 24px -> --space-6, 32px -> --space-7, etc.), value-for-value. Prioritize the worst inline-style offenders (EventSignupForm, PricingCalculator, SchnuppertageSection, AktuellesClient). Genuinely off-grid magic numbers tuned by subtraction (150px, 46/50px hero pad hacks, 120/140/200) are left untouched in this slice and flagged for the deferred alignment follow-up — do not re-express them if doing so would move a pixel.
acceptanceCriteria: A complete --space-1..12 scale exists and legacy --spacing-* names alias onto it; nothing that referenced a legacy name changes value
On-scale raw-px spacing in globals.css and the prioritized components now uses tokens equal to the same pixel value
Off-grid magic numbers are catalogued as deferred (not altered); no spacing element moves versus baseline
Screenshot parity across key pages incl. the form pages; full suite green
slices.blockedBy: Collapse to a single token source of truth

slices.title: Section vertical-rhythm tokens
slices.whatToBuild: Unify the section-rhythm vocabulary as names for current values. Define --section-gap (container vertical padding) and --section-gap-sm (gap between stacked sections) and apply them wherever a section currently sets vertical rhythm — but only where the current computed value already equals the token, so no section's breathing room changes. Where a context currently uses a genuinely different rhythm (e.g. home-main-content fixed 64px vs .cms-sections clamp), keep that context on a token carrying its present value rather than forcibly harmonizing (harmonizing rhythms is a perceptible change -> deferred). This slice gives the rhythm one named authority without altering any page's spacing.
acceptanceCriteria: --section-gap / --section-gap-sm tokens exist and are applied where they equal the current rendered rhythm
Contexts with a currently-different rhythm are tokenized to their present value, not changed; any genuine harmonization is logged as a deferred follow-up
No section's vertical spacing shifts versus baseline at the tested breakpoints
alignment + abos-shell-alignment + hero-shell-alignment tests pass; screenshot parity + full suite green
slices.blockedBy: Complete spacing scale + route raw-px through it

slices.title: Button primitive + delete duplicate .cta-button + shared ButtonVariant
slices.whatToBuild: Collapse the three primary-button implementations into one primitive, reproducing every call site's current look, and delete the provably-dead duplicate CSS. Build a single Button primitive over the existing .btn base with a variant union (primary | secondary | orange) and an explicit organic flag, then route CTA, all six form submit buttons, Hero, and EventsSection through it — each rendering exactly the classes it renders today (organic where it is organic now, plain where it is plain now, .btn-orange where used now). Delete the .cta-button ruleset, which is byte-for-byte identical to .btn.btn-primary, and point the components that used it at the primitive. Replace the open button-variant string type with the shared ButtonVariant union so the data model, CSS, and (future ACF) options agree. This is the single button primitive that maps to one ACF button block in the rebuild.
acceptanceCriteria: One Button primitive backs CTA, all six forms, Hero, and EventsSection; each button renders the identical class set / hover behavior it has today (organic vs non-organic preserved per current site)
The duplicate .cta-button ruleset is removed and no element loses styling (proven by parity, since it equaled .btn.btn-primary)
button variant is typed as a shared 'primary'|'secondary'|'orange' union across the type layer, the primitive, and the registry; .btn-orange is reachable through the typed variant
Screenshot parity on every page containing a button; full suite green
slices.blockedBy: Non-brand color token layer: neutrals, surfaces, borders, semantic state

slices.title: SectionHeading primitive across both render paths
slices.whatToBuild: Unify the two divergent section-heading systems behind one primitive without changing either path's current output. Extract a SectionHeading (eyebrow + title) component and use it in BOTH the class-based SectionRenderer path and the inline-styled renderHeader path of RegisteredSectionComponents. Because the two paths render differently today (class-based .cms-section-eyebrow + bare h2 vs inline eyebrow #5f6b7a/0.95rem and h2 clamp(2rem,3vw,3.6rem)), the primitive reproduces each via a variant so every existing heading stays pixel-identical — the actual visual unification of the two looks is a deferred design decision. Also merge the two conflicting .cms-section-eyebrow rules (the later one at ~L6312 silently wins today) into a single rule that keeps the currently-winning appearance, replacing its hardcoded #4C6F44 with the equivalent brand token. This primitive is the future ACF section-header sub-block.
acceptanceCriteria: A single SectionHeading component renders headings on both SectionRenderer and RegisteredSectionComponents paths; each call site's eyebrow/title stays byte-equal to baseline via variants
The duplicate .cms-section-eyebrow rules are merged into one that preserves the currently-winning styling; its hardcoded green hex becomes a token of the same value
No CMS or hardcoded page heading changes appearance; the two-looks-into-one unification is logged as a deferred follow-up
section-renderer + heading-contract tests pass; screenshot parity + full suite green
slices.blockedBy: Type scale + weights + line-heights + font-family truth fix

slices.title: FormField / input primitives across all six forms
slices.whatToBuild: Replace the three incompatible form-field patterns with one primitive set, reproducing each form's current rendering. Build FormField (label + error) wrapping TextInput / TextArea / SelectField / Checkbox on a single CSS baseline driven by input tokens (--input-radius, --input-pad, --input-border) set to current values, then migrate all six forms onto it: the .form-group + bare-input forms, MembershipForm's Bootstrap .form-control/.is-invalid variant, and EventSignupForm's ~15 inline-styled inputs. Each field must render with the same padding/border/radius and the same error presentation it has today (the inline EventSignupForm values become the token values; MembershipForm's validation look is preserved as a variant until the deferred visual unification). This is the ACF form-field block set for the rebuild.
acceptanceCriteria: All six forms render through the FormField/input primitives; EventSignupForm's inline style objects are removed in favour of a class using tokens equal to those inline values
MembershipForm validation and the bare-input forms keep their current appearance and error display (preserved as variants); no field shifts size or border
Input tokens (--input-radius/--input-pad/--input-border) exist at current values and are the single source for field styling
membership-validation + forms tests pass; screenshot parity of every form incl. error states; full suite green
slices.blockedBy: Complete spacing scale + route raw-px through it, Non-brand color token layer: neutrals, surfaces, borders, semantic state

slices.title: Card primitive + card tokens
slices.whatToBuild: Consolidate the seven card treatments into one primitive with variants that reproduce each current look. Define --card-radius and --card-shadow at their current values and build a Card primitive with variant=bento|soft|outlined|plain, then refactor the fragmented implementations (bento-card usages, CardsGridBlock article, GroupCardsSection inline card, LinkTiles portal-tile, Membership summary-card, EventsSection past-event-tile, CardHeader) onto it. Each variant renders the radius/shadow/border its source renders today, so nothing changes visually; the goal is one component with a style-variant field, which becomes one ACF card block. Also remove the no-op ternary in CardsGridBlock where both branches of the title margin are identical.
acceptanceCriteria: A single Card primitive with bento/soft/outlined/plain variants backs the previously-separate card implementations; each rendered card matches its baseline pixels
--card-radius / --card-shadow tokens exist at current values and drive the primitive; the no-op title-margin ternary is removed with identical output
link-tiles + schnuppertage + relevant section tests pass; screenshot parity on all pages with cards; full suite green
slices.blockedBy: Non-brand color token layer: neutrals, surfaces, borders, semantic state, Complete spacing scale + route raw-px through it

slices.title: Modal shell primitive
slices.whatToBuild: Extract one Modal shell (overlay + panel + sticky header + close) and have both current dialogs consume it, reproducing their current appearance. SchnuppertageSection hand-rolls a fixed-position modal entirely in inline styles, duplicating the dedicated ItemDetailModal; extract a shared Modal (open, onClose, title) whose overlay/panel/close styling equals what those two render today, then route both through it. Remove the ~70 lines of inline modal styling from SchnuppertageSection in favour of the shell. No change to how either modal looks or behaves; this yields one dialog/interaction pattern for the rebuild.
acceptanceCriteria: A single Modal shell backs both SchnuppertageSection and ItemDetailModal; both open/close and render identically to baseline
SchnuppertageSection's inline modal styling is removed and replaced by the shell with equal computed styles
schnuppertage-section + related interaction tests pass; screenshot parity of both dialogs open; full suite green
slices.blockedBy: Complete spacing scale + route raw-px through it

slices.title: De-hardcode RegisteredSectionComponents + enable hex-literal guard
slices.whatToBuild: Land the final de-hardcode and lock the door so coherence cannot regress. Route the ~41 inline style objects and ~13 hardcoded hexes in RegisteredSectionComponents (#4b5563 x10, #111827, #f5f2e9, #8ab272, #d97706, #5f6b7a, #d5dfcf, etc.) and its repeated per-block margin '0 auto 80px' through the tokens and primitives established earlier — each mapped to a token of the same current value and rendered via a shared block wrapper (using the section-rhythm token) plus the shared SectionHeading/Button primitives. Then enable a lint guard (stylelint color-no-hex and/or an eslint no-restricted-syntax rule on style props) that fails CI on new raw hex in CSS/TSX, so the token discipline holds through the WP migration. Values are unchanged throughout; this is the slice that makes each block a thin, ACF-mappable renderer.
acceptanceCriteria: RegisteredSectionComponents blocks reference tokens/primitives instead of inline hex and ad-hoc margins; every block renders byte-equal to baseline
The repeated per-block margin is replaced by a shared block wrapper using the section-rhythm token, with identical spacing
A hex-literal lint guard is enabled and green on the now-clean tree, and fails on an introduced raw hex fixture
component-registry + section tests pass; screenshot parity on all CMS-rendered pages; full suite green
slices.blockedBy: Brand-color token layer (green / carrot / beet + tint), Non-brand color token layer: neutrals, surfaces, borders, semantic state, Section vertical-rhythm tokens, Button primitive + delete duplicate .cta-button + shared ButtonVariant, SectionHeading primitive across both render paths
